results.content: ### Anion Gap is a Predictor of Elevated Serum Lactate in Patients Diagnosed with Sepsis without Shock in the Emergency Department. **Material and Methods:** This is a retrospective study among patients with sepsis without shock admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary care, university hospital. There was poor discriminative performance of the anion gap to predict serum lactate >2 mmol/L (area under ROC is 0.65; 95%CI 0.58-0.72). **Conclusion:** An anion gap >12 mmol/L is not suitable for assessing lactate >2 mmol/L; however, an anion gap >18 mmol/L can predict serum lactate >4 mmol/L in patients with sepsis who had mean arterial pressure (MAP) >65 mmHg. anion gap, sepsis, septic shock, serum lactate. Go to  My NCBI account settings  to confirm your email and then refresh this page. # Anion gap as a screening tool for elevated lactate in patients with an increased risk of developing sepsis in the Emergency Department. # Anion gap as a screening tool for elevated lactate in patients with an increased risk of developing sepsis in the Emergency Department. The objective of this study was to determine if a readily available anion gap (AG) could be used as a surrogate marker for abnormal lactate level in Emergency Department (ED) patients at risk for sepsis. The initial basic chemistry panels, calculated AG, and lactate levels drawn in the ED were collected. **Conclusion:**  This study suggests that an elevated AG obtained in the ED is a moderately sensitive and specific means to detect elevated lactate levels in ED patients at risk for sepsis.
